item.title: Japan’s 40-Year Yield Rises 10 Basis Points on Inflation Fears
item.description: Japan’s 40-year government bond yield rose 10 basis points, as investors remain unconvinced that the nation’s central bank will tighten policy fast enough to quell inflation.

item.title: Tech Stocks Face Investor Skepticism as Rally Stalls and Profit Estimates Rise
item.description: The earnings season is confirming worries that the technology rally had gone too far, with investors now harder to please and reluctant to buy into rising profit estimates.

item.title: UK Retail Sales Beat Forecasts Again With Strong June Increase
item.description: UK retail sales defied expectations again with a surprisingly strong rise in June, as sunny weather and the World Cup outweighed any concern among shoppers over the cost of living.

item.title: Tanker Exits Red Sea Dark as Another China Ship Heads to Strait
item.description: A Greek tanker carrying Saudi crude exited the Red Sea with its transponder off, while another Chinese vessel headed toward Bab el-Mandeb as Houthi attacks heightened risks for commercial shipping.

item.title: FTSE 100 Live: UK Stocks Set to Underperform as Oil Pulls Back
item.description: FTSE 100 Live: UK Stocks Set to Underperform as Oil Pulls Back【原文：FTSE 100 Live: UK Stocks Set to Underperform as Oil Pulls Back】

item.title: India Activity Slows to Over Four-Year Low on Iran Risks
item.description: India’s economic activity slowed to its weakest pace in more than four years in July as renewed tensions in the Middle East weighed on demand and intensified inflationary pressures, a flash survey by HSBC Holdings Plc showed Friday.

item.title: China Rushes to Buy East Russian Oil as Middle East Risks Grow
item.description: Chinese buyers are snapping up Russia’s flagship ESPO crude weeks earlier than usual, as heightened risks to Middle East oil flows prompt refiners to secure supplies before they’re needed.

item.title: UK Pub Stocks Fall as Heat Wave Proves Too Hot For Football Fans
item.description: UK pub stocks slumped this week as a sales boost from the World Cup failed to offset the drag from a brutal heat wave and higher costs.

item.title: Nagel Says ECB in Good Position, Stays Quiet on Next Rate Move
item.description: The European Central Bank will be able to lean on a raft of fresh information in September when it next meets to discuss interest rates, according to Governing Council member Joachim Nagel.

item.title: China Set to Look Past Trump’s New Tariffs Before Xi Visit to US
item.description: Donald Trump’s new tariffs of 12.5% on China might irk Beijing without provoking a retaliation, even as the US president rebuilds a protectionist wall after the Supreme Court struck down his initial levies.

item.title: Dangote Prefers London Over Dubai for Listing of Cement Unit
item.description: Dangote Cement Plc prefers to list its cement business in London because it will be quicker to sell shares on the exchange in the UK than in Dubai, according to Mariya Dangote, a board member in the cement business.

item.title: Global Bonds Are Reeling as Oil Surge Renews Inflation Threat
item.description: Global bonds are being pummeled by the latest resurgence in energy prices, delivering losses to investors who bet the worst of this year’s rout was over and teeing up credibility tests for central bankers.

item.title: Kyiv’s Strikes Battering Russian Economy Hang Over Rate Decision
item.description: Russian businesses are grappling with the bleakest conditions since the early months of the war on Ukraine, putting the central bank in a bind as it weighs a pause in its yearlong easing cycle that would prolong punishing borrowing costs.

item.title: BOE Bond Sales Decision Complicated by Burnham Yield Surge
item.description: Only last month, Andrew Bailey again insisted quantitative tightening is here to stay. The Bank of England governor has been adamant the UK central bank needs to keep slashing its bond holdings to clear the decks for the next crisis and take interest-rate risk off its balance sheet.

item.title: Korean Stocks Sink as Chipmakers Drop on Middle East, China IPO
item.description: South Korean stocks fell as funds cut exposure to chipmakers after overnight losses in US peers, while factoring in a Chinese rival’s imminent share sale and rising Middle East tensions.

item.title: Metals Fluctuate as Middle East Escalation Keep Bulls in Check
item.description: Base metals fluctuated at the end of the week as the threat of an escalating conflict in the Middle East — and more turbulence for the global economy — kept a lid on optimism.

item.title: India’s Markets Shrug Off Student Protests for Now
item.description: Student protests in India’s capital, a political headache for Prime Minister Narendra Modi, aren’t reflecting in the country’s financial markets.

item.title: Wheat Extends July Rally as War Risks Stoke Fears Over Supply
item.description: Wheat resumed its rally after a brief bout of profit-taking, as escalating geopolitical tensions and worsening weather in key producing regions continued to stoke supply concerns.

item.title: Malaysia Sells First Dollar Bonds in Five Years as Fuel Subsidy Bill Rises
item.description: Malaysia raised $1.5 billion in its first dollar bond sale in five years, bolstering funding as the Southeast Asian nation grapples with a fuel subsidy bill that’s likely to more than double from an initial goal due to the Iran war.

item.title: India’s SEBI Mulls Letting Portfolio Managers Invest Clients’ Money Overseas
item.description: SEBI proposes allowing investment in overseas securities and IPO-bound firms, among others.

item.title: Manipal Health Seeks to Raise Up to $960 Million in India IPO
item.description: Manipal Health Enterprises Ltd. is seeking to raise as much as 92.7 billion rupees ($960 million) in an initial public offering, continuing a run of sizable share sales in India.

item.title: Asian Allies Push Back Against Trump’s Forced-Labor Tariffs
item.description: Asian nations have described the Trump administration’s latest tariffs as baseless and unjustified, while stopping short of any retaliatory moves.

item.title: China’s Gold Imports Surge After International Prices Slump
item.description: Chinese gold imports rose to a two-year high in June, underscoring resilient demand in the world’s biggest bullion market after a plunge in international prices.

item.title: Chinese Stock Turnover Shrinks as Sentiment Cools on Tech Sector
item.description: Chinese daily stock turnover dropped to the lowest level in over three months, as investors shun the nation’s technology sector.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama Says to Take Bold FX Steps Decisively as Needed
item.description: Japanese authorities will take bold steps to counter moves in the currency market decisively as needed, and a US Treasury report issued overnight underscores a shared view that excessive currency moves are undesirable, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said.

item.title: Trump to Take Up Manila’s Concerns With Xi, Philippines Says
item.description: US President Donald Trump assured Philippine leader Ferdinand Marcos Jr. that he would take up Manila’s concerns when he meets with Chinese President Xi Jinping, the Southeast Asian nation said.

item.title: SK Hynix, Samsung and Kioxia Face Pivotal Earnings Test on AI Swings
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. and Samsung Electronics Co. are set to test investor appetite for memory chips as South Korea’s stock market — now a bellwether for global AI sentiment — grapples with violent swings driven by leveraged chip bets.

item.title: PHP/USD: Philippine Peso Falls to Fresh Record Low as Oil Advances
item.description: The Philippine peso fell to a fresh record low as oil prices climbed, boosting pressure on the central bank to intervene as markets eye 62 as the next key level.

item.title: Macquarie’s First Woman CEO Departs With a $339 Million Stake
item.description: Shemara Wikramanayake is stepping down as head of Macquarie Group Ltd. after leading the Australian financial conglomerate to bumper profits and a record high share price. For that she will be richly rewarded, making her one of the best-paid female bank executives in the world.

item.title: Modi Seeks to Calm Anger in Rare Video as India Protests Widen
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi made a fresh bid to calm mounting anger over examination paper leaks as students prepared nationwide protests on Friday, with demands growing for the education minister to step down.
